tagline: Clinch River communities trace the changing civic geography of Russell County
intro: St. Paul and Castlewood lie along the Clinch River in the Appalachian Mountains. At St. Paul, the Sugar Hill section of Clinch River State Park includes 400 acres and more than two miles of river access.

Russell County’s first court met in William Robinson’s house at Castle’s Woods in May 1786. Lebanon was founded in 1818 in an effort to establish a new county seat. The courthouse there has been in use since 1874.

St. Paul’s business district contains commercial buildings largely dating from the 1920s through the 1950s. Castlewood carries the shortened form of Castle’s Woods, adopted by the United States Postal Service in the late nineteenth century. Lebanon remains Russell County’s seat.

moments.title: St. Paul
moments.text: Students made a local wetland the focus of a reclamation and education project in St. Paul. The Wetlands Estonoa Project was initiated and run by students, and received a federal grant to build the Vencil Learning Center. The river also anchors Sugar Hill, a 400-acre unit of Clinch River State Park with more than two miles of river access. Dedicated in 2021, the park is planned as a chain of properties linked by canoe and kayak access along the Clinch. That full network remains a development plan. At Sugar Hill, cultural remains include an eighteenth-century French settlement.

moments.title: Castlewood
moments.text: Castlewood spent six years as an incorporated town, then reversed the decision. In 1991 it established a mayor and six-member council, seeking to attract industry after coal-mine losses by improving infrastructure. New property taxes financed a town hall. Voters later elected a government that dismantled incorporation in 1997. The name itself had already changed: the United States Postal Service shortened Castle’s Woods to Castlewood in the late nineteenth century. The community lies beside the Clinch River in far southwestern Virginia. In an earlier civic role, the county’s first court met here in William Robinson’s house in May 1786.

moments.title: Lebanon
moments.text: Lebanon was founded in 1818 to create a new seat for Russell County, and it retains that role. The county’s first court had met in a house at Castle’s Woods in 1786; the present Lebanon courthouse has served since 1874. A later layer of the town’s architecture appears at the Stephen B. Quillen House, built in 1912. The two-story frame dwelling uses a Queen Anne design, with a steep hipped roof and lower cross gables. A porch wraps the first floor, while the doors and windows have simple detailing.
